subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For macOS gateway exec, should allowlisted shell-shaped commands auto-execute only when OpenClaw can build a bound enforced command plan, or should the current plan-miss prompt behavior become the documented contract?
rationale: The user impact is real, but the current gate is deliberately tied to a security boundary that prevents raw shell execution when executable binding or shell expansion cannot be made stable.

options.title: Repair safe planner-bound cases
options.body: Teach the macOS/POSIX planner to bind common safe shapes such as absolute argv and narrowly modeled tilde/path forms, keep prompt-only behavior for unbound shell payloads, and add Darwin regression proof.

options.title: Document fail-closed limitation
options.body: Keep the current approval gate and update exec approval docs plus warning text so operators can convert automation to argv-clean commands intentionally.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell commands
options.body: Let allowlist matches run even when no enforced command can be materialized, accepting a broader shell-resolution trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Repair safe planner-bound cases
recommendation.body: Teach the macOS/POSIX planner to bind common safe shapes such as absolute argv and narrowly modeled tilde/path forms, keep prompt-only behavior for unbound shell payloads, and add Darwin regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent macOS shell-wrapper allowlist ownership signal is the merged hardening work in this area.
